Academic Yearly Report
Student Name: Henry Mu Student ID: 19903
Grade: Grade 7
Dear Parents,
On behalf of the entire IB teaching team at KCISEC, we are pleased to present your child’s academic yearly report for
the academic year of 2025 – 2026.
It is required for our school to report to parents and students how students are progressing using the MYP assessment
criteria which are used by other IB World Schools worldwide. All the work of our students is internally assessed by our
teachers. The KCISEC IB teaching team has been working closely together designing relevant and authentic
assignments, tests and projects which reflect the IB philosophy. We have also been collaboratively designing IB rubrics
and sharing them with the students. KCISEC IB teachers are required to assess each criterion at least twice per
academic year. When judgments on the various tasks have been made, our teachers will be in a position to determine
the final level of achievement. The final level of achievement for each criterion must then be added together to give a
total for each subject for each student. Please be assured that our teachers have been explaining the IB grading
system to your children with each individual assignment. The rubrics provide clarity around the teachers’ expectations
and allow the students to understand their progress in distinct areas of a subject, rather than only general progress.
We believe you will find this report effective in providing you with a clear understanding of your child’s current progress.
We also hope that you are able to see the areas where focus and attention will be placed once school resumes after
the summer break. Should you find that you have questions or comments related to your child’s report, please feel free
to contact us for any further clarification. Your participation and partnership with us has been integral to ensuring that
the education your child receives is first-rate. As always, we look forward to continuing our work together.
Sincerely yours,
Dr. Kate Lin
Principal of KCISEC IB
Programmes

===== PAGE 2 =====
IB Learner Profile
Inquirers We nurture our curiosity, developing skills for inquiry and research. We know how to learn independently and with
others. We learn with enthusiasm and sustain our love of learning throughout life.
Knowledgeable We develop and use conceptual understanding, exploring knowledge across a range of disciplines. We engage
with issues and ideas that have local and global significance.
Thinkers We use critical and creative thinking skills to analyse and take responsible action on complex problems. We
exercise initiative in making reasoned, ethical decisions.
Communicators We express ourselves confidently and creatively in more than one language and in many ways. We collaborate
effectively, listening carefully to the perspectives of other individuals and groups.
Principled We act with integrity and honesty, with a strong sense of fairness and justice, and with respect for the dignity and
rights of people everywhere. We take responsibility for our actions and their consequences.
Open-minded We critically appreciate our own cultures and personal histories, as well as the values and traditions of others. We
seek and evaluate a range of points of view, and we are willing to grow from the experience.
Caring We show empathy, compassion and respect. We have a commitment to service, and we act to make a positive
difference in the lives of others and in the world around us.
Risk-takers We approach uncertainty with forethought and determination; we work independently and cooperatively to explore
(Courageous) new ideas and innovative strategies. We are resourceful and resilient in the face of challenges and change.
Balanced We understand the importance of balancing different aspects of our lives — intellectual, physical, (spiritual) and
emotional — to achieve well-being for ourselves and others. We recognise our interdependence with other people
and with the world in which we live.
Reflective We thoughtfully consider the world and our own ideas and experience. We work to understand our strengths and
weaknesses in order to support our learning and personal development.
Henry Mu

Grade Descriptors
Final Grade Descriptor
Produces high-quality, frequently innovative work. Communicates comprehensive, nuanced understanding of concepts
7 and contexts. Consistently demonstrates sophisticated critical and creative thinking. Frequently transfers knowledge
and skills with independence and expertise in a variety of complex classroom and real-world situations.
Produces high-quality, occasionally innovative work. Communicates extensive understanding of concepts and
6 contexts. Demonstrates critical and creative thinking, frequently with sophistication. Uses knowledge and skills in
familiar and unfamiliar classroom and realworld situations, often with independence.
Produces generally high-quality work. Communicates secure understanding of concepts and contexts. Demonstrates
5 critical and creative thinking, sometimes with sophistication. Uses knowledge and skills in familiar classroom and real-
world situations and, with support, some unfamiliar real-world situations.
Produces good-quality work. Communicates basic understanding of most concepts and contexts with few
4 misunderstandings and minor gaps. Often demonstrates basic critical and creative thinking. Uses knowledge and skills
with some flexibility in familiar classroom situations, but requires support in unfamiliar situations.
Produces work of an acceptable quality. Communicates basic understanding of many concepts and contexts, with
3 occasionally significant misunderstandings or gaps. Begins to demonstrate some basic critical and creative thinking. Is
often inflexible in the use of knowledge and skills, requiring support even in familiar classroom situations.
Produces work of limited quality. Expresses misunderstandings or significant gaps in understanding for many
2 concepts and contexts. Infrequently demonstrates critical or creative thinking. Generally inflexible in the use of
knowledge and skills, infrequently applying knowledge and skills.
Produces work of very limited quality. Conveys many significant misunderstandings or lacks understanding of most
1 concepts and contexts. Very rarely demonstrates critical or creative thinking. Very inflexible, rarely using knowledge or
skills.

Comments:
Henry has been a very helpful, courteous and hard-working student. He is academically capable and consistently
achieves strong exam results. Meanwhile, Henry actively takes part in in-class discussions and performs outstandingly
when analyzing activity guidelines during group tasks. When finishing homework, he is able to draw inferences flexibly
and develop deeper reflections than most classmates. Keep up the fantastic work! Henry already has solid subject
knowledge and proficient English skills. Based on his current exam performance, he has attained top-level results in
this course and is encouraged to explore relevant extracurricular content for further enrichment.
In this academic year, we went through four units. For Unit One, we studied ecosystems by understanding different
biomes. More importantly, students explored endangered animals and understood the importance of protecting
biodiversity. For Unit Two, we explored civilizations between 500 and 1500 CE. Students were encouraged to explore
the daily life and social development of different civilizations. For Unit Three, students learned about culture and
festivals. They studied how rituals and activities changed due to social and technological development. For the last
unit, we explored globalization. Students learned about the impacts of globalization on the world economy, including
its positive influences and negative consequences. Through learning these four units, students were able to practice
skills of collecting information, analyzing sources, organizing sources, and presenting information to different

about cells and their functions, chemical concepts such as atoms, ions, the periodic table, and physical and chemical

work together to maintain balance and support life. Throughout the year, students developed their scientific inquiry
skills by conducting investigations, analyzing data, and improving their ability to communicate scientific understanding
clearly and effectively.

Comments:
Henry is a highly motivated and independent learner who consistently demonstrates an excellent standard of
achievement in Visual Arts. He is a positive role model for his classmates through his strong focus during lessons,
consistent completion of work, and enthusiastic approach towards learning and creative exploration.
During Semester 1, students explored how artists communicate identity, emotion, and meaning through both 2D and
3D artworks. In Unit 1, students created mixed media self-portraits that explored personal identity through symbolism,
colour, composition, and artistic style. In Unit 2, students shifted from 2D artworks into 3D sculptural processes by
designing and constructing expressive symbolic masks using papier-mâché and mixed media techniques. Throughout
the semester, students developed their creative-thinking skills, craftsmanship, and understanding of how artists refine
and communicate ideas and identity through visual art.
Henry demonstrated exceptional skill in selecting and critically evaluating research information relevant to his
investigations. He thoughtfully connected cultural mask traditions to the statement of inquiry by explaining how
principles, discoveries, symbolism, and visual culture influenced mask design and function. Henry also effectively
compared and contrasted different masks, demonstrating strong analytical skills and deep understanding of artistic
meaning. His open-minded curiosity and willingness to experiment with different media significantly strengthened the
quality of his artwork and investigations.
To continue developing, Henry could strengthen his artistic reflection further by discussing more specific examples
from his creative process, such as how experimentation, composition changes, or media exploration improved his final

Comments:
Henry has been a very helpful, courteous, polite, and hard-working student throughout the year.
This year in Grade 7 PE, students started by becoming mini fitness experts! They learned all about how fitness and
nutrition fuel our bodies and worked together to plan a fitness session for a young athlete. It was exciting to see them
apply their learning to a real-world challenge. Next, we put our teamwork skills to the test with invasion games.
Students discovered that communicating clearly and collaborating with teammates is the secret to success. They also
took time to reflect on how they were learning and growing as team players. When the second semester arrived, it was
time to get moving with aerobics. Students explored different styles, from high-energy to more controlled routines, and
focused on performing each one effectively. Their creativity and willingness to try new things really shone through. We
finished the year strong with Colpbol and Field Hockey. These international games required students to think fast,
communicate in big groups, and work together toward a common goal. It was a fantastic way to bring all their skills
together!
He is an enthusiastic learner who thrives in group activities and genuinely enjoys socializing with peers while staying on
task.
Henry is a highly motivated independent learner who is to be commended for a consistently high level of achievement
across all criteria. He is a role model for other students in terms of his ability to focus on the task, apply skills
effectively and consistently complete work.

Design: G7 Design Carla Pepler
Learner Profile:Knowledgeable
MYP Assessment Criteria Achievement Level Maximum
A: Inquiring and analysing
Henry
i. explains the need for a solution to a problem
ii. constructs a research plan, which states and prioritizes the primary and secondary research 6 8
needed to develop a solution to the problem, with some guidance
iii. describes a group of similar products that inspire a solution to the problem
iv. develops a design brief, which outlines the findings of relevant research.
B: Developing ideas
Henry
i. develops design specifications, which identify the success criteria for the design of a solution
ii. presents a range of feasible design ideas, using an appropriate medium(s) and explains key
features, which can be interpreted by others 6 8
iii. presents the chosen design and outlines the main reasons for its selection with reference to the
design specification
iv. develops accurate planning drawings/diagrams and lists requirements for the creation of the
chosen solution.
C: Creating the solution
Henry
i. constructs a plan, which considers time and resources, sufficient for peers to be able to follow to
create the solution 6 8
ii. demonstrates competent technical skills when making the solution
iii. creates the solution, which functions as intended and is presented appropriately
iv. outlines changes made to the chosen design and plan when making the solution.
D: Evaluating
Henry
i. describes detailed and relevant testing methods, which generate accurate data, to measure the
success of the solution
7 8
ii. explains the success of the solution against the design specification based on authentic product
testing
iii. describes how the solution could be improved
iv. describes the impact of the solution on the client/target audience.
